minutes.headline: Committee advanced a new K-6 bus-application policy to a second read, opened five school choice seats, and approved a concession stand monitor.
minutes.summary: The School Committee heard public comment on SEL, the equity audit and the school calendar's religious holidays. It took budget Q&A, a quarterly budget update, an Esser grant reallocation proposal, a snack shack upgrade update, a mid-year assessment presentation and a first read of the transportation policy. Votes covered a line-item transfer, a concession stand monitor position, school choice seats, and first read of policies.

public_comment.topic: Busing for every parent, opposition to mandatory SEL, questions on equity audit report, cost and contract, and a list of demands including seeking a new superintendent.
Asked that the school calendar and events consider Jewish and other religious observances and support students.
A member praised the PTO over a dance ticket dispute and rejected claims the schools tolerate bullying (member speaking during the last public comment period).

votes.motion: Revise agenda to include the November 16th minutes
Approve the January 18th minutes (deferred, members absent)
Approve line item transfer from Turkey Hill presented by Mr Cassidy
Approve the concession stand monitor position (permission to post)
Open five school choice seats for grade nine class of 2027, carry forward one unfilled seat, and allow grade 11-12 students who move to remain
Accept first readings of policies 3701-01, 3701-02 and 3701-03
Go to executive session at 10:28 pm and adjourn following

budget_items.what_was_said: Funds left in math, guidance and science supply accounts moved to buy an interactive screen for art instruction.
Budget is on target; some negative balances will be zeroed by transfers already voted, a nursing line to be covered by a DPH grant, and a technology deficit tied to an e-rate billing error.
Encumbrances explain why the visible balance looks small; about a hundred thousand remains to get through the year.

Projected spending leaves a surplus, due to unused insurance budgeting, salary savings and moves to local budget; a reallocation to i-Ready, Chromebooks and moving two positions to ESSER 3 is proposed and tabled for public comment.
Completed plumbing and equipment work cost just under a stated amount; pending upgrades cost a further amount, with a donation expected to cover them.
Hourly position funded from the facility revolving account; groups charged at a set hourly rate when spot checks occur.
School choice students count in Chapter 70 headcount; tuition is reconciled at state level; the school choice account pays for course reimbursements and food service health insurance.
Superintendent said reading intervention, tutors and i-Ready are grant funded and may have to move into the local budget when ESSER ends.
Town manager proposed funding the first six items including Turkey Hill doors and security upgrades; fire alarm item unfunded pending tax abatement holdback.

transfers.description: From Turkey Hill math supplies, guidance supplies and science supplies to a touch view interactive screen for art

Another budget question and answer period set for the first meeting in March.
ESSER amendment to be posted for public comment and brought back February 15th or March 1st.
Superintendent's assistant may update the acronym list as new acronyms arise.

Bus policy to return for another first read with revisions: grade language, waiver wording for K-6 who miss May 1 deadline, emergency application as the appeal route.
Food policies and concessions policy return as second reads next meeting.
Possible workshop or legal update on bullying considered for a future meeting.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to open five school choice seats for the grade nine class of 2027 and carry forward one unfilled seat.
It sent the K-6 bus-application policy back for another first read, with revisions to grade language, waiver wording for missed deadlines and the appeal route.
It approved posting a concession stand monitor position, paid hourly from the facility revolving account, and approved a line-item transfer at Turkey Hill.
An ESSER grant reallocation was tabled for public comment, to return February 15th or March 1st.
The quarterly update said the FY23 budget is on target, and the superintendent said grant-funded reading help may move into the local budget when ESSER ends.

why_it_matters: The bus policy sets who gets K-6 busing and what happens to families who miss the May 1 application deadline, so the revised version will decide how those families apply.
Reading intervention, tutors and i-Ready are paid from grants that end with ESSER, so keeping them would mean moving them into the local budget, which is funded mostly by taxes.
watch_next: The ESSER reallocation returns February 15th or March 1st after public comment.
The revised bus policy returns for another first read, and the food and concession policies return for second reads at the next meeting.
